name: Adafruit 381 waterproof DS18B20 temperature probe
description: Pre-wired, waterproofed DS18B20 1-Wire digital thermometer in a stainless steel tube Ø6 x 30 mm on a 91 cm, Ø4 mm PVC cable, three wires (red VDD 3.0-5.5 V, blue/black GND, yellow/white DQ). -55 to +125 C sensor (keep under 100 C for the PVC cable), +-0.5 C from -10 to +85 C, 9-12 bit, 750 ms max per 12-bit conversion, unique 64-bit ROM code. Supplied with a 4.7 kOhm DQ pull-up resistor. Not IP rated.

params.description: Probe: 'Red connects to 3-5V'. DS18B20 VDD (TO-92 pin 3): 'Optional VDD. VDD must be grounded for operation in parasite power mode.'

params.note: current_draw is the 1.5 mA active maximum (1 mA typ, VDD = 5 V), drawn during temperature conversions and EEPROM writes: up to 750 ms per 12-bit conversion. Standby is 750 nA typ, 1000 nA max up to +70 C (typically 3 uA at +125 C); keep DQ within 0.3 V of GND or VDD for the lowest standby current.
params.source: https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/DS18B20.pdf (DC Electrical Characteristics) (IDD, IDDS, Notes 7-9); https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/DS18B20.pdf (AC Electrical Characteristics, tCONV)

params.description: Probe: three-wire 'Blue/Black connects to ground' (four-wire build: black). DS18B20 GND (TO-92 pin 1): 'Ground'.

Probe: three-wire 'Yellow/White is data' (four-wire build: white). DS18B20 DQ (TO-92 pin 2): 'Data Input/Output. Open-drain 1-Wire interface pin. Also provides power to the device when used in parasite power mode.'

params.note: Open-drain; the bus needs an external pull-up of about 5 kOhm to VPU (3.0 V to VDD), and Adafruit supplies a 4.7 kOhm resistor 'required as a pullup from the DATA to VCC line'. Idle high; holding the bus low for more than 480 us resets every device on it. Levels: VIL max 0.8 V, VIH min 2.2 V (local power) up to the lower of 5.5 V or VDD + 0.3 V; sinks 4.0 mA min at 0.4 V; DQ input current 5 uA typ; 25 pF max. Time slots 60-120 us, reset low 480 us min.
source: https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/DS18B20.pdf (1-Wire Bus System; DC and AC Electrical Characteristics)

params.note: Each DS18B20 has a unique 64-bit ROM code with family code 28h, so several probes can share one DQ line; the master finds them with Search ROM and addresses them with Match ROM (or Skip ROM with a single device). There is no fixed address to configure.

interfaces.name: Cable end: 3 stripped wires (VDD red, GND blue/black, DQ yellow/white)

params.note: Three-wire build: 'Red connects to 3-5V, Blue/Black connects to ground and Yellow/White is data' (src_product). The photos show the jacket stripped back and stranded copper ends stripped and untinned, no connector (src_photos). Position order follows Adafruit's listing; there is no pin 1.

Some probes ship with four wires: 'Red connects to 3-5V, Black connects to ground and White is data. The copper wire is soldered to the wire shielding.' Check the wire count on receipt; on a four-wire probe the bare copper drain wire is the shield (ground it at the board end or leave it unconnected; Adafruit gives no recommendation).

interfaces.name: Stainless tube Ø6 x 30 mm (sensing end, seal surface)

params.note: Stainless steel tube 6 mm diameter by 30 mm long, waterproofed with heat shrink. Adafruit: 'Not for use in salt water or other corrosive environments. These are not IP rated, and are not guaranteed for long term/high pressure usage.' A rod seal or gland closes on the exposed tube; the heat-shrink sleeve behind it is about the tube diameter or larger, so insert the probe tip first.

interfaces.name: Cable exit (Ø4 mm PVC jacket leaves the heat shrink)

params.note: Cable is 36" / 91 cm long, 4 mm diameter, jacketed in PVC (keep under 100 C). It may be cut to length; the wires inside are re-stripped at the cut. Wire gauge is not stated.

artifacts.name: DS18B20 datasheet copy linked by Adafruit (REV 042208)

supply_current.condition: standby up to +70 C; active at VDD = 5 V

metadata.nominal_voltage_note: 3.3 V is the smart-bottle rail; any VDD from 3.0 to 5.5 V is in range

package.name: Waterproof probe, stainless tube Ø6 x 30 mm, 3-wire cable
package.assumption: Adafruit names no package; the name is built from its cable specs. The three terminals are the wire ends, designated VDD, GND and DQ (the wire colours vary by batch).

metadata.dimensions_note: overall about 940 mm: the 30 mm tube plus the 910 mm cable (whether the 91 cm includes the tube is not stated); width and height are the tube diameter
metadata.shipping_weight_note: shipping weight from the Adafruit product record, packaging and the resistor included; not the probe's mass

metadata.operating_note: DS18B20 operating range -55 to +125 C; Adafruit: 'While the sensor is good up to 125°C the cable is jacketed in PVC so we suggest keeping it under 100°C.'
source: https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/DS18B20.pdf (Absolute Maximum Ratings; DC Electrical Characteristics, tERR)

params.drift_note: 1000-hour stress test at +125 C, VDD = 5.5 V (datasheet Note 11)
params.alarm: nonvolatile TH / TL alarm registers, Alarm Search [ECh]

params.temperature_note: sensor -55 to +125 C; probe kept under 100 C for the PVC cable
params.environment: not IP rated; not for salt water or corrosive environments; not guaranteed for long-term or high-pressure use

params.note: The DS18B20 can run without VDD: tie the red VDD wire to GND and power the device through DQ. The master must then switch a strong pull-up onto DQ within 10 us of a Convert T [44h] or Copy Scratchpad [48h] and hold it for the conversion (up to 750 ms) or 10 ms write, and cannot poll for completion. Parasite power is not recommended above +100 C. With VDD powered (as modelled) the bus stays free during conversions.

Adafruit points to the Dallas Temperature Control Arduino library with the OneWire library. Query time is less than 750 ms at 12 bits; lower resolutions convert faster (93.75 ms at 9 bits). Adafruit tests that the sensors are genuine Maxim DS18B20s (since January 2021).

fields: whether the 91 cm includes the tube
params.note: Adafruit dimensions only the tube and the cable, and publishes only a shipping weight (27.2 g, with packaging and resistor).

The Adafruit product page has no CAD link (its Downloads list only the DS18B20 datasheet), and the adafruit/Adafruit_CAD_Parts GitHub repository has no model for 381 or any DS18B20 probe. Geometry is generated from the product page dimensions and the product photos (library/cad/py/catalog/adafruit-381-ds18b20-probe.py).

params.value: three-wire build: red VDD, blue or black GND, yellow or white DQ; no shield or drain wire
params.reason: Adafruit ships three-wire and four-wire builds under product 381 and does not say which arrives. The smart-bottle brief assumes the three-wire build. A four-wire probe adds a copper drain wire soldered to the shield (wire_ends usage_note).

params.value: the 30 mm is the exposed stainless length, from the closed tip to the heat-shrink sleeve
params.reason: Adafruit states 'Stainless steel tube 6mm diameter by 30mm long' without saying whether the tube continues under the heat shrink. Photo 381-02 scaled by the 6 mm tube shows about 33 mm of exposed stainless, which agrees within the photo's precision.

params.value: sleeve behind the tube Ø6.3 x 24 mm, then a sleeve over the cable Ø4.8 x 25 mm
params.reason: Not dimensioned. Read from photo 381-02 scaled by the 6 mm tube (25 px) and the 4 mm cable (16 px), about 0.245 mm/px: the first sleeve is about the tube diameter and 99 px long, the second 19-20 px wide and 103 px long.

params.value: jacket drawn 50 mm (not 910 mm); three wires broken out 35 mm beyond the jacket, insulation Ø1.5 mm, stranded conductor drawn as a Ø0.6 mm rod stripped 15 mm; wires on a 0.9 mm radius in the jacket, red at +Y, GND at 210 deg, DQ at 330 deg
params.reason: The cable is drawn as a stub because a project cuts it to its routed length (the wire-end frames sit at the drawn ends, not 910 mm away); the cable_length parameter states the delivered length. Breakout and wire sizes are read from photos 381-01 and 381-02; the gauge is not stated.
